title: GLM 5.3 FlashX Legal Launch: Specs and Speed Test
summary: GLM 5.3 FlashX Legal launch was evaluated on three automation tasks. Results show performance on legal workflows to help you decide if it fits your needs.
body_markdown:
## GLM 5.3 FlashX Legal cost and speed


Judge GLM 5.3 FlashX Legal against the model you already run (we tested openai/gpt-5.4-mini, an older OpenAI model, as the baseline) on what each task costs and how long it takes. The listed price alone won't tell you what lands on the invoice.


### Listed price versus measured cost


A per-token price is what the maker publishes. What you pay is a per-task cost, after counting the model's prompts, retries and output length.


Those can diverge, and a client billed on the per-task figure is the one who absorbs the difference. Use the maker's pricing page for the listed side, and the test runs for the measured side.


> A per-token price is what the maker publishes. What you pay is a per-task cost, after counting the model's prompts, retries and output length.


Do not read much into the price history: earlier flagship GLM models have changed their output prices over time. That history is context only. It's not this model's price, and it shouldn't set your expectations for it.


### GLM 5.3 FlashX Legal speed in testing


Whether a step can sit inside a live workflow or has to be queued comes down to latency. A cheaper run that takes noticeably longer can still cost you in worker time and client waiting.


The test measured seconds per task for both models, so the comparison is like for like.


It shows measured cost per task and measured latency for each model across the three tasks, allowing you to balance performance against cost based on your requirements.


Treat three tasks as a small sample. It shows direction, not a guarantee, so rerun it on your own documents before you reprice anything.
